question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{36}∼N(4,{18}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $36$ from a normal population, calculate $P(|\overset{―}{X}|<2.07).$ *Hint: Value tables of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.02\,$$\,0.03\,$$\,0.04\,$
$\,-0.7\,$ $\,0.2358\,$ $\,0.2327\,$ $\,0.2296\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2676\,$ $\,0.2643\,$ $\,0.2611\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.3015\,$ $\,0.2981\,$ $\,0.2946\,$

$z$$\,0.02\,$$\,0.03\,$$\,0.04\,$
$\,-2.0\,$ $\,0.0217\,$ $\,0.0212\,$ $\,0.0207\,$
$\,-1.9\,$ $\,0.0274\,$ $\,0.0268\,$ $\,0.0262\,$
$\,-1.8\,$ $\,0.0344\,$ $\,0.0336\,$ $\,0.0329\,$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(4,\frac{{18}^{2}}{36}) \\  & ∼N(4,9).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(|\overset{―}{X}|<2.07).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|<2.07) & =P(-2.07<\overset{―}{X}<2.07) \\  & =P(\frac{-2.07-4}{\sqrt{9}}<Z<\frac{2.07-4}{\sqrt{9}}) \\  & =P(-2.02<Z<-0.64) \\  & =Φ(-0.64)-Φ(-2.02)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.64) & =0.2611, \\ Φ(-2.02) & =0.0217.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|<2.07) & =Φ(-0.64)-Φ(-2.02) \\  & =0.2611-0.0217 \\  & =0.2394.\end{aligned}
$$
